# DSH Service Manager
**One page for every MCP server and skill in DeepSeek Harness.**
Add, edit, enable, disable and delete MCP servers without touching YAML · browse your skills · trans
late their English summaries with your own model.
English · 简体中文
## Why
DeepSeek Harness ships no MCP management UI. Adding a server means hand-writing YAML; finding out wh
ether it connected means going back to a session and trying. Skills live as files on disk with Engli
sh summaries you read once and forget.
This plugin adds the missing page. It **never edits your DSH configuration files** — it loads its ow
n file through the official `cordis:include` mechanism, so `cordis.patch.yml` stays exactly as you w
hrough the official `cordis:include` mechanism, so `cordis.patch.yml` stays exactly as you wrote it.

## Features
### MCP servers

- **Full CRUD without YAML** — add, edit, delete, and toggle servers from a table
- **Expand to the

tool list** — every tool a server registers, one line each, with the full description on hover
- **T
ool drawer** — summary on top, parameter table below; parameter descriptions are translated, paramet

er names stay English because they are the identifiers you actually type
- **Reconnect is visible**
— saving triggers a background include refresh; the page polls the reconnect state instead of leavin

g you staring at a spinner
- **`${ENV_VAR}` references** — keep secrets in the environment, not in t

at a spinner
- **`${ENV_VAR}` references** — keep secrets in the environment, not in the config file
### Skills

- **Browse everything DSH can see**, with each skill's summary and body kept as two layers
- **Trans
late summaries with your own model** — the picker lists every provider × model configured in DSH, de

faults to your default model, and remembers the choice
- **`译文 / 原文` toggle** for the whole list, **

↻** to re-translate a single card, and a batch re-translate in the toolbar
- **Cached on disk** — th

e second visit is zero requests
- **Failure is visible** — when the model cannot deliver, the card s

ays `机翻` (machine translation) rather than pretending it worked
- **Delete** a skill from the page
-
**Reveal in file manager** — the folder button next to the path in the drawer selects that `SKILL.m
in file manager** — the folder button next to the path in the drawer selects that `SKILL.md` for you
> Translations only change what you read. `SKILL.md` is never modified — the model still receives th
e original English prompt.
### Agent tool
The plugin also registers an `mcp_service` tool, so you can say *"install the filesystem MCP"* in a
conversation instead of switching pages.
| Action | What it does | Needs approval |

| `list` | Servers, transport, status, tool count | No |
| `install` | Add or update a server | **Ye

s** |
| `remove` | Delete a server | **Yes** |
| `enable` / `disable` | Toggle a server | No |
Approval goes through DSH's one-shot authorization interface. A rejection, a cancellation, or no ava
ilable answerer **leaves the configuration untouched** — it fails closed. Malformed arguments are re
jected *before* the prompt, so an unusable request never interrupts you.
### Both themes
Everything is built on DSH's design tokens, so light and dark follow the app automatically.

## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness `>= 0.2.0-rc.1 < 0.3.0`
- `pnpm` on `PATH` (the plugin manager uses it)
- Desktop
app on Windows, macOS or Linux

> ⚠️ Before reinsta
lling the same package from a *different* source (say, a local directory you installed earlier), rem
ove the leftover under `node_modules` first — otherwise you get `ERR_PNPM_EPERM`. See FAQ.
## What it writes
Everything the plugin owns lives in your profile directory. Nothing else is touched.
| Path | What it is |

| `<profile>/mcp-servers.yml` | Generated MCP rows — the `cordis:include` target |
| `<profile>/.dsh

-service-manager/servers.json` | Source of truth for the server list |
| `<profile>/.dsh-service-man

ager/translations.json` | Translation cache, keyed by a hash of the source text |
| `<profile>/.dsh-

service-manager/settings.json` | Your model choice |
| `<profile>/.dsh-service-manager/diagnostics.j
son` | Health of the agent tool and the load-time probe |
`<profile>` is `~/.dsh/profiles/<name>` — on Windows, `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\profiles\desktop`.
## Security boundaries

- Writes **only** the files listed above
- **Never** modifies `cordis.patch.yml`, `cordis.yml` or `.

credentials.yaml`
- Secrets are best written as `${ENV_NAME}` and read from the environment at load

time, so the config file holds no plaintext
- The Host half runs **inside the DSH process**, outside
the workspace sandbox — check the source before installing anything from a stranger
## How it works
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The page reads and writes through routes registered with `ctx.connection.fetch.register` under `/api
/service-manager/*`. After a write, the plugin refreshes the include subtree so the MCP bridge recon
nects; the client polls that state rather than blocking.
Translation goes through `ctx.get("llm").stream(...)` with the model you picked, and is written back
to `translations.json` so it survives restarts.
## Compatibility

- DSH `>= 0.2.0-rc.1 < 0.3.0`
- Windows / macOS / Linux desktop
- Both themes, automatically
- No bu
ild step, no runtime dependencies
